IMD weather alert today: ‘Red’ alert for heavy rains in Keralam, Tamil Nadu, ‘severe’ cyclone to hit Andhra on Oct 28 According to the latest IMD update, the weather system is very likely to move nearly southwards today, intensify into a Deep Depression, and then gradually recurve west-northwestwards over the Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal by October 26 morning. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the depression over the Bay of Bengal will rapidly intensify into a Deep Depression on Sunday, October 25. This marks the first major escalation of a weather system that is on a trajectory to transform into a “very severe” cyclonic storm before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast next week. According to the latest IMD update, the system is very likely to move nearly southwards today, intensify into a Deep Depression, and then gradually recurve west-northwestwards over the Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal by October 26 morning. It will likely develop “into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal around the morning of 27 October 2026,” IMD said. As of 2330 hours IST on October 24, the weather agency said the depression was centred over the East Central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal. It had been moving southeastwards at a speed of 8 kmph over the preceding six hours. The Met office pinpointed its location at approximately 470 km north-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands), 860 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 950 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 1060 km east of Machilipatnam, and 1130 km east of Bapatla. Following today's escalation into a Deep Depression, the IMD forecasts a rapid, multi-stage intensification process: October 26: Continuing its west-northwestward trajectory, the system is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the Eastcentral and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal by the morning. October 27: The storm is expected to upgrade into a severe cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by the morning. The IMD warned that the system will ultimately peak as a very severe cyclonic storm. It is projected to reach the Westcentral Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast by the morning of October 28. The very severe cyclonic storm is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the forenoon of October 28. During landfall, coastal regions should brace for maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, with violent gusts reaching up to 140 kmph. Under the influence of this system, the Met Department forecast rainfall in parts of the southern state from October 26 to 29. It said thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are expected at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam, and Rayalaseema on October 26, 27, and 28, followed by scattered heavy to very heavy rain, with extremely heavy rain likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on October 27. For October 28, the Met Department forecast scattered heavy to very heavy rain with extremely heavy rain likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam. On October 29, it predicted heavy rain in parts of Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam. The IMD has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall in five Kerala districts on Sunday and Monday. Malappuram, Kozhikode, and Wayanad districts are under a red alert on October 25, while Idukki and Palakkad are placed under the same category the next day, according to the IMD's latest update. An orange alert has been issued for Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod on Saturday, indicating the possibility of very heavy rainfall in isolated areas. Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki and Ernakulam are under yellow alert for heavy rainfall on the day. The weather agency has also issued a red alert for Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, predicting heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, while coastal Karnataka may also witness intense showers. Before joining LiveMint, Arshdeep served as a Senior Sub‑Editor at Business Standard and earlier as a Sub‑Editor at Asian News International (ANI). Her experience spans live news flows, enterprise features, and multi‑platform packaging.

At Mint, she regularly writes explainers, quick takes, and visuals‑led stories that are optimized for search and social, while maintaining the publication’s standards for accuracy and clarity. She collaborates closely with editors and the audience team to frame angles that resonate with readers in India and abroad, and to translate complex developments into accessible, high‑impact journalism.

Arshdeep's academic training underpins her interest towards policy and markets. She earned an MA in Economics from Panjab University and holds a Post‑Graduate Diploma in Broadcast Journalism from the India Today Media Institute (ITMI). This blend of economics and broadcast storytelling informs her coverage of public policy, elections, macro themes, and the consumer‑internet zeitgeist.

Arshdeep is based in New Delhi, where she tracks breaking developments and longer‑horizon storylines that shape public discourse.
